examples.ko: 동생이 엄마한테 제 비밀을 다 고해바쳤어요.
examples.en: My little brother snitched all my secrets to Mom.

examples.ko: 누가 선생님께 고해바쳤는지 궁금해요.
examples.en: I wonder who told on us to the teacher.

examples.ko: 친구가 고해바칠까 봐 걱정돼서 말을 못 했어요.
examples.en: I was afraid my friend would tell on me, so I couldn't say anything.

examples.ko: 고해바치는 사람은 친구들에게 인기가 없어요.
examples.en: People who tattle aren't popular with their friends.

examples.ko: 언니한테 고해바쳐도 소용없어요, 제가 먼저 말할 거예요.
examples.en: Telling my sister is pointless; I'll tell her first.

examples.ko: 친구를 몰래 고해바치다니 정말 실망이에요.
examples.en: I'm really disappointed that you secretly told on your friend.

explain: '일러바치다', '고자질하다'와 거의 같은 뜻이에요. 남의 잘못을 윗사람에게 몰래 말하는 것이라서 말하는 사람을 비난하는 느낌이 있어요. 일상 대화에서는 '일러바치다'도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: My friend told the teacher about my mistake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻이고 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, and more common in everyday talk.

phrases.en: It's hard to trust a friend who tattles.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남의 잘못을 몰래 말하는 사람을 비난하는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Carries a tone of blaming the person who tells on others.

phrases.example: 제가 말한 건 엄마한테 고해바치지 마세요.
phrases.en: Please don't tell Mom what I said.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비밀을 지켜 달라고 부탁할 때 쓰는 부정 명령형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative request form, used to ask someone to keep a secret.

explain_en: It is nearly the same as '일러바치다' and '고자질하다'. Since it means secretly telling someone in authority about another person's fault, it carries a tone of blame toward the teller. In everyday talk '일러바치다' is also common.

t90.ax: I wonder who told on us to the teacher.

en: to play a joke on; to play a trick on

examples.ko: 형이 자꾸 저를 골려서 화가 났어요.
examples.en: My older brother keeps teasing me, and I got angry.

examples.ko: 친구들이 생일 파티에서 저를 골렸어요.
examples.en: My friends played a trick on me at the birthday party.

examples.ko: 동생을 골리지 말고 같이 놀아 주세요.
examples.en: Don't tease your little brother, play with him.

examples.ko: 그 선생님은 학생들을 골리는 것을 좋아하세요.
examples.en: That teacher likes to tease his students.

examples.ko: 장난으로 골렸는데 진짜 화낼 줄은 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I was just teasing, but I didn't think he would get really angry.

examples.ko: 친구를 골려 주려고 가짜 편지를 썼어요.
examples.en: I wrote a fake letter to play a trick on my friend.

explain: '놀리다'와 비슷하지만 일부러 약을 올려서 상대를 당황하거나 화나게 만든다는 느낌이 더 강해요. 반드시 '~를 골리다'처럼 대상이 필요해요. 정도가 심하면 괴롭힘처럼 들릴 수 있어요.

phrases.en: My older brother teased me as a joke.
phrases.nuance_ko: '골리다'에 '주다'를 붙여 장난으로 상대를 약 올렸다는 느낌을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '주다' to 골리다 gives the feel of playfully getting a rise out of someone.

phrases.en: Please don't tease your friend so much.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그만하라고 부탁하거나 말릴 때 쓰는 존댓말 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a polite way to ask someone to stop teasing.

phrases.en: My friends make fun of my name.
phrases.nuance_ko: '골리다'보다 뜻이 넓고 덜 짓궂어서 가벼운 장난에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is broader and milder than 골리다 and also works for light joking.

explain_en: It is similar to '놀리다', but it feels more like deliberately provoking someone to fluster or annoy them. It always needs an object, as in '~를 골리다'. If it goes too far, it can sound like bullying.

examples.ko: 아버지는 어머니 앞에서는 공처가가 돼요.
examples.en: In front of my mother, my father becomes henpecked.

examples.ko: 친구들은 저를 공처가라고 놀려요.
examples.en: My friends tease me by calling me henpecked.

examples.ko: 공처가 남편이 나오는 코미디를 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched a comedy with a henpecked husband in it.

examples.ko: 그는 겉으로는 센 척해도 사실 공처가예요.
examples.en: He acts tough on the outside, but he is actually henpecked.

examples.ko: 공처가 소리를 들어도 우리 집은 평화로워요.
examples.en: Even if I'm called henpecked, our home is peaceful.

examples.ko: 삼촌은 소문난 공처가라서 늘 일찍 집에 가요.
examples.en: My uncle is a well-known henpecked husband, so he always goes home early.

explain: 아내를 몹시 무서워하거나 아내 말을 잘 따르는 남편을 조금 놀리듯 부르는 말이에요. 반대로 아내를 많이 사랑하는 남편은 '애처가'라고 해요. 본인에게 쓰면 농담이 되지만 남에게 직접 쓰면 실례일 수 있어요.

phrases.en: My friend is totally henpecked.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체 서술형이라 농담처럼 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Polite sentence ending, used jokingly.

phrases.example: 아버지는 공처가라서 어머니 말을 잘 들으세요.
phrases.en: My father is henpecked, so he listens well to my mother.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 말하는 연결형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connective form that gives a reason.

phrases.en: That actor is famous for being henpecked.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주변에서 그렇게 알고 있다는 뜻이라 농담처럼 가볍게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says people widely know him as such; used lightly, like a joke.

explain_en: It is a teasing word for a husband who is very afraid of his wife or does what she says. A husband who loves his wife a lot is called '애처가', the contrasting word. Using it about yourself can be a joke, but saying it directly to someone else can be rude.

en: to be freaky; to be bad-tempered

examples.ko: 우리 할아버지는 성격이 좀 괴팍하셔서 말을 걸기 어려워요.
examples.en: My grandfather is a bit cranky, so it's hard to talk to him.

examples.ko: 그 교수님은 괴팍하지만 학생들을 아끼세요.
examples.en: That professor is eccentric, but he cares about his students.

examples.ko: 괴팍한 취미를 가진 사람이 우리 동네에 살아요.
examples.en: A person with an eccentric hobby lives in our neighborhood.

examples.ko: 나이가 들수록 성미가 괴팍해지는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people become more cranky as they get older.

examples.ko: 그 작가는 괴팍하기로 유명해요.
examples.en: That writer is famous for being eccentric.

examples.ko: 제 상사는 괴팍해서 기분을 맞추기가 힘들어요.
examples.en: My boss is so cranky that it's hard to keep him happy.

explain: 주로 사람의 성격이나 성미, 취미가 까다롭고 별나서 맞추기 어렵다는 느낌일 때 써요. 윗사람에게 쓸 때는 '괴팍하시다'처럼 '-시-'를 넣어요. 단순히 재미있게 특이한 사람은 '독특하다'나 '특이하다'가 더 어울려요.

phrases.example: 괴팍한 성격 때문에 친구가 많지 않아요.
phrases.en: He doesn't have many friends because of his difficult personality.
phrases.nuance_ko: 까다롭고 별난 성격을 말할 때 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for a picky, eccentric personality.

phrases.en: The boss is a bit eccentric.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람에게 쓸 때는 '-시-'를 넣어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-si-' when talking about someone of higher status.

phrases.en: He looks cranky, but he has a warm heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로 까다로워 보인다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means someone seems difficult on the surface.

explain_en: It is mainly used for a person's temperament or hobbies when they are fussy and peculiar and hard to deal with. For someone older or senior, add '-시-', as in '괴팍하시다'. For someone who is simply interestingly unusual, '독특하다' or '특이하다' fits better.

en: to coax; to talk someone into

examples.ko: 동생이 아빠를 구워삶아서 용돈을 받아 냈어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling sweet-talked Dad into giving pocket money.

examples.ko: 아무리 구워삶아도 엄마는 허락하지 않으셨어요.
examples.en: No matter how much I buttered her up, Mom didn't give permission.

examples.ko: 그는 상사를 구워삶는 데 선수예요.
examples.en: He's an expert at buttering up his boss.

examples.ko: 영업사원이 손님을 구워삶으려고 계속 칭찬했어요.
examples.en: The salesperson kept complimenting the customer to win them over.

examples.ko: 친구를 구워삶아 숙제를 대신 시킬 생각이에요?
examples.en: Are you planning to sweet-talk your friend into doing your homework?

examples.ko: 언니가 나를 구워삶았는데 결국 넘어갔어요.
examples.en: My older sister buttered me up, and I ended up giving in.

explain: 듣기 좋은 말이나 행동으로 상대를 내 뜻대로 움직이게 하는 느낌이에요. '구슬리다'와 비슷하지만 의도가 더 뻔히 보이고 약간 얄미운 뉘앙스가 있어요. 주로 말할 때 써요.

phrases.en: He was trying to sweet-talk me, so I was careful.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-으려고 하다'로 하려는 의도를 말하고, 경계하는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: -으려고 하다 shows intent, with a wary tone.

phrases.example: 언니가 엄마를 살살 구워삶아서 허락을 받았어요.
phrases.en: My older sister sweet-talked Mom into giving permission.
phrases.nuance_ko: '살살'로 슬슬 비위를 맞추는 모습을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: 살살 shows the gradual flattering of someone.

phrases.en: The teacher coaxed the student into giving a presentation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말인데, 구워삶다보다 조금 약하고 부드러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word, a little milder and softer than 구워삶다.

explain_en: It carries the feel of steering someone your way with pleasant words or actions. It is similar to '구슬리다', but the intent is more obvious and it has a slightly sly, cheeky tone. It is mostly used in speech.

t90.ax: He's an expert at buttering up his boss.

examples.ko: 사극에서 궁녀 역할을 맡은 배우가 인기를 얻었어요.
examples.en: The actress who played a palace maid in the period drama became popular.

examples.ko: 조선 시대 궁녀들은 왕과 왕비를 가까이에서 모셨어요.
examples.en: Palace women in the Joseon era served the king and queen up close.

examples.ko: 궁녀가 되면 평생 궁궐 밖으로 나가기 어려웠대요.
examples.en: I heard that once you became a palace maid, it was hard to leave the palace for life.

examples.ko: 박물관에서 궁녀의 옷차림을 재현한 전시를 봤어요.
examples.en: At the museum I saw an exhibit recreating a palace maid's clothing.

examples.ko: 드라마 속 궁녀는 왕의 비밀을 알아내고 몹시 놀라요.
examples.en: The palace maid in the drama finds out the king's secret and is shocked.

examples.ko: 궁녀들이 궁궐 마당을 바쁘게 오가는 장면이 나와요.
examples.en: There is a scene where palace maids hurry back and forth across the palace yard.

explain: 궁궐에서 일하던 여성을 가리키는 말이라 사극이나 역사 이야기에서 자주 들어요. 사극에서는 '상궁', '나인' 같은 말도 같이 나오니 함께 알아 두면 좋아요. 지금은 쓰지 않는 역사 속 신분이에요.

phrases.example: 그 소녀는 열두 살에 궁녀가 되었어요.
phrases.en: That girl became a court maid at the age of twelve.
phrases.nuance_ko: 역사 이야기에서 신분을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in historical stories to describe someone's position.

phrases.en: The court maids attended to the queen.
phrases.nuance_ko: 복수형으로 사극 장면을 설명할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The plural form, often used to describe historical drama scenes.

phrases.en: A sanggung is a senior who leads the court maids.
phrases.nuance_ko: 궁녀 중에서 지위가 높은 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a high-ranking woman among the palace women.

explain_en: It refers to women who worked in the royal palace, so you hear it often in period dramas and history stories. Words like '상궁' and '나인' also appear in those dramas, so it helps to learn them together. It is a historical status that no longer exists today.

examples.ko: 의사가 운동을 권유했어요.
examples.en: The doctor advised me to exercise.

examples.ko: 친구가 같이 여행 가자고 권유해서 가게 됐어요.
examples.en: A friend invited me on a trip, so I ended up going.

examples.ko: 점원이 새 상품을 계속 권유해서 부담스러웠어요.
examples.en: The clerk kept pushing new products, and it felt like pressure.

examples.ko: 선생님은 학생들에게 책 읽기를 권유하세요.
examples.en: The teacher encourages students to read books.

examples.ko: 억지로 권유하지는 않을게요.
examples.en: I won't force you to do it.

examples.ko: 부모님이 유학을 권유하셨어요.
examples.en: My parents urged me to study abroad.

explain: 상대가 어떤 일을 해 보도록 부드럽게 이끌 때 써요. '추천하다'는 좋은 것을 알려 주는 느낌이고, '권유하다'는 행동하도록 마음을 움직이는 느낌이에요. 강하게 시키면 '강요하다'예요.

phrases.en: Grandma offered me some fruit.
phrases.nuance_ko: '권유하다'와 뜻이 비슷하지만 더 쉬운 말이에요. 음식을 권할 때도 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning to '권유하다' but simpler, and natural also when offering food.

phrases.en: I joined the club after my friend encouraged me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 권유하는 사람이 아니라 받는 사람 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the viewpoint of the person receiving the suggestion rather than the one giving it.

phrases.en: I quit drinking following the doctor's advice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대의 권유대로 행동했다는 뜻으로 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing meaning one acted as the other person suggested.

explain_en: Used when gently steering someone toward doing something. '추천하다' is about pointing out something good; '권유하다' is about moving the person to act. Pushing hard is '강요하다' (force).

t90.ax: I won't force you to do it.

examples.ko: 친구의 꼬임에 넘어가서 수업을 빼먹었어요.
examples.en: I fell for my friend's coaxing and skipped class.

examples.ko: 그 달콤한 꼬임이 사실은 거짓말이었어요.
examples.en: That sweet temptation was actually a lie.

examples.ko: 아이들은 어른의 꼬임을 쉽게 알아채지 못해요.
examples.en: Children can't easily notice an adult's enticement.

examples.ko: 누구의 꼬임으로 이런 일을 했는지 말해 보세요.
examples.en: Tell me whose enticement led you to do this.

examples.ko: 꼬임은 처음에는 좋은 말처럼 들려요.
examples.en: Enticement sounds like nice words at first.

examples.ko: 그 광고의 꼬임 때문에 필요 없는 물건을 샀어요.
examples.en: That ad tempted me into buying something I didn't need.

explain: '꼬임에 넘어가다', '꼬임에 빠지다'처럼 짝말로 외워 두면 편해요. 동사는 '꼬드기다'이고, 일상 대화에서는 '꼬시다'라고도 해요. 같은 글자의 '꼬임'이 실이나 줄이 꼬인 상태를 가리킬 때도 있어요.

phrases.en: I fell for my sister's coaxing and did the dishes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 달콤한 말에 속아 하게 되는 상황을 말하는 대표 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The standard collocation for being tricked into doing something.

phrases.en: Be careful not to fall into a bad temptation.
phrases.nuance_ko: '넘어가다'보다 좋지 않은 유혹에 깊이 걸려드는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels like getting more deeply caught in a bad lure than 넘어가다.

phrases.en: Don't be fooled by sweet-talking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 듣기 좋은 말로 꾀는 것을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to luring with pleasant-sounding words.

explain_en: It is easiest to learn as a set phrase, like '꼬임에 넘어가다' or '꼬임에 빠지다'. The related verb is '꼬드기다', and in everyday talk people also say '꼬시다'. The same word '꼬임' can also mean the state of a thread or rope being twisted.

t90.ax: That sweet temptation was actually a lie.

examples.ko: 아버지는 평생 농사꾼으로 사셨어요.
examples.en: My father lived his whole life as a farmer.

examples.ko: 저 농사꾼 아저씨는 일 솜씨가 대단해요.
examples.en: That farmer uncle is really skilled at his work.

examples.ko: 농사꾼의 손은 거칠지만 따뜻해요.
examples.en: A farmer's hands are rough but warm.

examples.ko: 저도 나중에 농사꾼이 되고 싶어요.
examples.en: I also want to become a farmer someday.

examples.ko: 그는 서울 사람이지만 농사꾼처럼 일해요.
examples.en: He is from Seoul but works like a farmer.

examples.ko: 농사꾼은 날씨에 민감할 수밖에 없어요.
examples.en: Farmers can't help being sensitive to the weather.

explain: 일상 대화에서 편하게 쓰는 말이에요. 격식 있는 자리나 글에서는 '농부'나 '농민'이 더 무난해요. '-꾼'은 어떤 일을 잘하거나 즐겨 하는 사람 뒤에 붙는 말이에요.

phrases.en: My grandfather is a farmer.
phrases.nuance_ko: '농사꾼'보다 격식 있고 무난해서 누구에게나 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: More neutral and polite than 농사꾼, so it is safe in any situation.

phrases.en: The farmers brought rice to the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 글에서 농사짓는 사람들을 함께 부를 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in news and writing for farming people as a group.

phrases.en: My father is a born farmer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 농사 솜씨가 아주 좋은 사람을 칭찬하는 말로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise someone who is naturally good at farming.

explain_en: It is a casual, everyday word. In formal settings or writing, '농부' or '농민' is safer. The suffix '-꾼' attaches to someone who does a particular job or does it habitually.

t90.ax: A farmer's hands are rough but warm.

examples.ko: 동생은 능청맞게 모르는 척했어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling slyly pretended not to know.

examples.ko: 능청맞은 얼굴로 거짓말을 해서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was shocked that he lied with such a straight face.

examples.ko: 어쩜 그렇게 능청맞아요? 하나도 안 떨리나 봐요.
examples.en: How can you be so brazen? You don't seem nervous at all.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 능청맞아서 누구도 화를 내지 못해요.
examples.en: That child is so cheeky that no one can get angry at him.

examples.ko: 능청맞던 친구가 오늘은 솔직하게 말했어요.
examples.en: My usually sly friend spoke honestly today.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 생각보다 능청맞지 않아서 금방 들켰어요.
examples.en: He wasn't as cunning as I thought, so he got caught right away.

explain: '능청스럽다'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 쓰는데, 조금 더 구어체 느낌이에요. 모르는 척하는 태도를 얄밉거나 재미있게 볼 때 써요. 활용은 '능청맞아요, 능청맞은, 능청맞게'처럼 규칙적이에요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is really sly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 성격을 말하는 기본 해요체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic polite form for describing someone's character.

phrases.example: 그는 아무 일도 없었다는 듯 능청맞게 대답했어요.
phrases.en: He answered slyly, as if nothing had happened.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게' 형태로 동작이 어떤지 말해 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: The -게 form tells how an action is done.

phrases.example: 그 아이는 능청스러워서 화를 낼 수가 없어요.
phrases.en: That child is so sly that I can't get angry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 거의 같은 뜻이고, 조금 더 널리 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning and slightly more widely used.

explain_en: It is used almost the same as '능청스럽다' but feels a little more colloquial. You use it when you see someone's feigned innocence as cheeky or amusing. It conjugates regularly: '능청맞아요, 능청맞은, 능청맞게'.

t90.ax: My usually sly friend spoke honestly today.

en: good handwriting; person with good penmanship

examples.ko: 선생님은 달필로 유명하세요.
examples.en: The teacher is famous for beautiful handwriting.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 글씨를 잘 써서 달필이에요.
examples.en: That friend writes very well; he has fine handwriting.

examples.ko: 달필인 사람이 쓴 편지는 읽기도 좋아요.
examples.en: A letter written by someone with fine handwriting is pleasant to read.

examples.ko: 아버지는 달필이라서 축하 글을 자주 부탁받으세요.
examples.en: My father has fine handwriting, so he is often asked to write congratulatory messages.

examples.ko: 저는 달필은 아니지만 또박또박 쓰려고 해요.
examples.en: I don't have fine handwriting, but I try to write neatly.

examples.ko: 달필이 아니어도 정성이 담긴 카드는 좋아요.
examples.en: Even without fine handwriting, a card written with care is lovely.

explain: 글씨를 잘 쓰는 것, 또는 그런 사람을 말해요. 반대말은 '악필'이에요. 보통 대화에서는 '글씨를 잘 쓰다'라고 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: My father has beautiful handwriting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 글씨를 잘 쓴다고 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a person as having good handwriting.

phrases.en: My older sister writes neatly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 달필보다 일상 대화에서 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural in daily conversation than 달필.

phrases.en: My teacher is famous for having beautiful handwriting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글씨를 잘 쓰는 것으로 알려진 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for someone known for their fine handwriting.
phrases.en_equiv: to be known for good handwriting

explain_en: It refers to writing well by hand, or to a person who does. Its opposite is '악필' (poor handwriting). In ordinary conversation people more often say '글씨를 잘 쓰다'.

examples.ko: 아버지는 사나이 대장부처럼 씩씩하게 일하세요.
examples.en: My father works with vigor like a true man.

examples.ko: 대장부답게 약속은 꼭 지키세요.
examples.en: Keep your promises like a real man.

examples.ko: 그 정도 일에 우는 건 대장부가 할 짓이 아니에요.
examples.en: Crying over something like that is not what a real man does.

examples.ko: 할머니는 여자지만 대장부라고 불리셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother was a woman, but people called her bold and big-hearted like a real man.

examples.ko: 내가 대장부라면 이 일을 반드시 해낼 거예요.
examples.en: If I were a real man, I would surely pull this off.

examples.ko: 대장부의 기개로 어려움을 이겨 냈어요.
examples.en: He overcame the hardship with the spirit of a stout-hearted man.

explain: 씩씩하고 마음이 넓고 당당한 남자를 가리키는 옛 느낌의 말이에요. 요즘은 성격이 시원시원한 여성에게 '대장부 같다'고도 하고, '여장부'라는 말도 있어요. 칭찬으로 쓰지만 성별 틀을 담은 말이라 쓸 때 조심하는 사람도 있어요.

phrases.en: He is a big-hearted, true man.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛 느낌이 나는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common, somewhat old-fashioned pairing.

phrases.en: Like a man of character, he admitted his mistake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 당당하고 책임감 있는 행동을 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise confident, responsible behavior.

phrases.en: My aunt is a bold, big-hearted woman.
phrases.nuance_ko: 씩씩하고 마음 넓은 여성을 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a brave, big-hearted woman.

explain_en: It is an old-fashioned word for a manly man who is spirited, broad-hearted, and dignified. Today people also say '대장부 같다' about a frank, bold woman, and there is the word '여장부' too. It is meant as praise, but some people are careful with it because it carries gender expectations.

en: to be shrewd; to be impudent; to be wicked

examples.ko: 다섯 살짜리가 어른에게 따지다니 참 맹랑해요.
examples.en: A five-year-old arguing with an adult is quite cheeky.

examples.ko: 맹랑한 꼬마 덕분에 다들 웃었어요.
examples.en: Everyone laughed thanks to the cheeky little kid.

examples.ko: 어린아이가 말을 어찌나 맹랑하게 하는지 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was surprised at how boldly the little child spoke.

examples.ko: 신입이 사장님께 먼저 악수를 청하다니 맹랑하네요.
examples.en: A new hire offering a handshake to the boss first is pretty bold.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 보기와 달리 맹랑했어요.
examples.en: That child was cheekier than he looked.

examples.ko: 맹랑하다고 혼내기도 하지만 귀엽기도 해요.
examples.en: I scold him for being cheeky, but he's cute too.

explain: 주로 어린아이나 아랫사람이 나이에 비해 당돌하고 야무지게 굴 때 써요. 놀라움이 섞여 있어서 '당돌하다'와 비슷하지만 귀엽다는 느낌이 들 때도 있어요.

phrases.example: 저 맹랑한 아이가 어른처럼 말해서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
phrases.en: I was surprised because that cheeky child spoke like an adult.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나이에 비해 당돌한 아이를 놀라워하면서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with surprise for a child who is bold for their age.

phrases.example: 동생이 선생님께 맹랑하게 굴어서 제가 사과했어요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling acted cheeky toward the teacher, so I apologized.
phrases.nuance_ko: 당돌하게 행동하는 모습을 말하고, 때로는 버릇없다는 느낌도 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes bold behavior and sometimes feels a bit rude.

phrases.example: 작은 아이가 큰 소리로 따지니까 맹랑해 보였어요.
phrases.en: The small child looked cheeky arguing in a loud voice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이나 행동을 보고 느낀 인상을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the impression you get from someone's look or behavior.

explain_en: It is mainly used when a child or junior person acts boldly and sharply beyond their age. It carries surprise, so it is similar to '당돌하다', and can sometimes feel endearing.

t90.ax: That child was cheekier than he looked.

examples.ko: 저는 무남독녀라서 어릴 때부터 형제가 없어 심심했어요.
examples.en: I'm an only daughter, so I was bored as a kid with no siblings.

examples.ko: 그 집 무남독녀가 올해 대학에 들어갔어요.
examples.en: The only daughter of that family got into university this year.

examples.ko: 무남독녀인 그녀는 부모님의 사랑을 듬뿍 받았어요.
examples.en: As an only daughter, she received plenty of love from her parents.

examples.ko: 드라마에서 주인공은 부잣집 무남독녀예요.
examples.en: In the drama, the main character is the only daughter of a rich family.

examples.ko: 무남독녀를 시집보내는 아버지의 마음은 어땠을까요?
examples.en: How might a father feel marrying off his only daughter?

examples.ko: 무남독녀로 자라서 혼자 노는 데 익숙해요.
examples.en: I grew up as an only daughter, so I'm used to playing alone.

explain: 아들 없이 딸 하나만 있는 집의 외동딸을 가리켜요. 일상에서는 '외동딸'이 훨씬 자연스럽고, '무남독녀'는 드라마나 소설, 약간 옛날식 말투에서 자주 나와요. 반대로 딸 없이 아들 하나뿐이면 '무녀독남'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 저는 외동딸이라서 부모님이 저를 많이 아끼세요.
phrases.en: I'm an only daughter, so my parents cherish me a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '무남독녀'보다 훨씬 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Much more natural in daily speech than 무남독녀.

phrases.example: 그녀는 무남독녀로 자라서 혼자 노는 데 익숙해요.
phrases.en: She grew up as an only daughter, so she is used to playing alone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 환경에서 자랐는지 말할 때 써요. 소설이나 드라마 같은 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the family one grew up in; sounds like a novel or drama.
phrases.en_equiv: to grow up as an only daughter

explain_en: It refers to the only daughter in a family with no sons and no other children. In everyday speech '외동딸' is much more natural, while '무남독녀' shows up in dramas, novels and slightly old-fashioned speech. The counterpart for an only son with no sisters is '무녀독남'.

t90.ax: How might a father feel marrying off his only daughter?
